## Open

### F-626 — INSERT IGNORE hides the foreign key that a submission violates

> _2026-10-28 · realm/blong-feedback · open_

feedback.session.add failed with 'Could not create the feedback_session row: a unique column is
already taken' while the table has only its primary key. coreResourceEnsure uses INSERT IGNORE, and
MySQL swallows a foreign-key violation under IGNORE the same way it swallows a duplicate: the row is
silently not inserted and the caller reports a unique conflict that does not exist. The real cause
was userResourceId: $meta.auth.actorId is the crockford rendering of the resource id, not a dashed
UUID, so uuidBuf turned it into the wrong sixteen bytes and the foreign key to core_resource
rejected it. actorBuf now tries hex, crockford and base64, in the same order as aclActorId in
core/blong-gogo/src/adapter/server/acl.ts. The tap flow passed all along because it runs
unauthenticated and stored a null actor.

### F-625 — A page handler in a top-level component folder never registers

> _2026-10-28 · realm/blong-feedback · open_

Writing the review page and its menu as handler() files under a top-level component/ folder looked
right, because component is a well-known layer, and it loaded without complaint: the composed menu
even gained the group once the portal answered portalConfigGet. The browser resolves a page as
component/`<method>` and a bare `<method>` is not found, so the folder has to be
browser/orchestrator/component/ — the group name is the prefix — and a portal config provider
belongs in browser/orchestrator/portal/, where the portal namespace exposes it as a bare name. The
realm's browser.ts globs browser/orchestrator/**/*.ts, so nothing else needed changing. Cost: two
probe runs and one Playwright failure reading 'Handler component/feedback.review not found' before
the naming rule was obvious.

## Resolved

### F-628 — A JSON column arrives already parsed, and JSON.parse on it throws

> _2026-10-29 · realm/blong-feedback · resolved_

feedback.session.items returned neither anchor nor callout while the database plainly held both. The
knex adapter hands a JSON column back as an object, not as text, so the reader's JSON.parse(value)
threw inside its own try/catch and answered undefined for every row — the probe that printed the raw
column showed an object where the code expected a string. parseBox now accepts either shape and
checks the four numbers, which is what a reader of a column whose storage type changed under it has
to do anyway. Cost: one temporary debug field and one probe run to see it, because the failure was
silent by design.

parseBox accepts a parsed object or text; the row type is unknown, and the review page now draws
both boxes because of it.

### F-630 — A flex item shrank under its picture and painted over the panel below

> _2026-10-29 · realm/blong-feedback · resolved_

At a 560 pixel window the review pages picture pane was shorter than its content, so the picture and
its callouts painted over the Generated prose panel: a flex item has flex-shrink 1 by default and
its children are not clipped by it. The visible symptom looked like z-index and cost a screenshot to
see at all. The panes row now carries flexShrink 0 so the outer column scrolls, which is also what
the request asked for.

Fixed: the panes row carries flexShrink 0, so the panes keep their height and the outer column
scrolls; verified in the staged story at 740x560.

### F-632 — A gateway params schema silently drops the fields it does not name

> _2026-10-29 · realm/blong-feedback · resolved_

The review page moved a callout and the box stayed where it was after a re-open; the wording of the
same call persisted, so the page looked half-broken. The adapter handler had been given a callout
parameter and the tap flow exercised it, but the tap flow calls the handler directly: the published
page goes through gateway/feedback/feedbackItemEdit.ts, whose validation schema listed only
sessionId, itemId, commentText and refinedText. Validation stripped callout and removed before the
adapter ran, the handler answered updated 0, and nothing anywhere reported a problem. The schema now
names both, and the Playwright spec asserts the rows after the drag, because it is the only test
that crosses the gateway. Lesson: adding a field to an adapter handler is not adding it to the API.

Fixed: the schema declares callout (four numbers) and removed (boolean); the spec now reads the rows
back after a drag and re-opens the session, and the tap flow covers the box, the close and the
restore against the handler.
